title: Romsey Primary School and Nursery: 10 July 2026
text:
Determination
Case references: VAR2736 and VAR2737
Admission Authority: Hampshire County Council for Romsey Primary
School and Nursery
Local Authority: Hampshire County Council
Date of decision: 10 July 2026
Determination
In accordance with section 88E of the School Standards and Framework Act 1998, I
approve the proposed variations to the admission arrangements determined by
Hampshire County Council for Romsey Primary School and Nursery, for 2025/26 and
for 2026/27.
I determine that for admission in 2025 the published admission number shall be 40.
I determine that for admission in 2026 the published admission number shall be 20.
The referral
1. Hampshire County Council (the Local Authority, the LA, and the Admission Authority)
has referred to the adjudicator a proposal for variations to the admission arrangements for
Romsey Primary School and Nursery (the School) for both 2025/26 and 2026/27 (the
Arrangements).
2. The School is a community school for children aged three to eleven in Romsey. It is
a co-educational school. The school is located in the town of Romsey north of
Southampton.
3. The Admission Authority for the School is the local authority (LA). As the LA is the
Admission Authority, both terms are used throughout this determination.
4. Parties to the request are the LA and the School.

5. The proposed variations are that the published admission number (PAN) for the
School should be as follows:
• 40 children for 2025/26.
• 20 children for 2026/27.
Jurisdiction and procedure
6. Section 88E of the School Standards and Framework Act 1998 (the Act) makes
provision for variations to determined arrangements. Paragraphs 3.6 and 3.7 of the School
Admissions Code (the Code) say (insofar as is relevant here):
“3.6 Once admission arrangements have been determined for a particular school year,
they cannot be revised by the admission authority unless such revision is necessary to
give effect to a mandatory requirement of this Code, admissions law, a determination
of the Adjudicator or any misprint in the admission arrangements. Admission
authorities may propose other variations where they consider such changes to be
necessary in view of a major change in circumstances. Such proposals must be
referred to the Schools Adjudicator for approval, and the appropriate bodies notified.
Where the local authority is the admission authority for a community or voluntary
controlled school, it must consult the governing body of the school before making any
reference.
3.7 Admission authorities must notify the appropriate bodies of all variations”.
7. The Arrangements were determined by the Admission Authority on 20 February
2024 (for 2025) and 14 February 2025 (for 2026).
8. The Admission Authority has provided me with confirmation that the appropriate
bodies have been notified of the proposed variations in line with the Code. An initial error
stating the proposed PAN was for 36 children for 2025/26 was amended later to the current
proposal of 40 children, and the appropriate bodies were informed of this. The LA has
provided me with confirmation that the governing body of the School has been consulted on
the proposed variations.
9. I find that the appropriate procedures were followed, and I am satisfied that the
proposed variations are within my jurisdiction.
10. In considering the variation request, I have had regard to all relevant legislation and
the Code.
11. The information I have considered in reaching my decision includes:
• the referral from the Admission Authority dated 22 May 2026 and supporting
documents;
2

• the determined Arrangements for 2025/26 and 2026/27 and the proposed
variations to those Arrangements;
• responses from the LA, and the School to my requests for further information;
• maps, including Google Maps and those showing the location of the School; and
• information available on the websites of .gov.uk. (including the ‘Get Information
About Schools’ (GIAS) and ‘Financial Benchmarking and Insights Tool’ (FBIT)
websites), the LA, and the School (including its Arrangements for 2025/26 and
2026/27) and Ofsted.
12. I would like to extend my thanks to the LA and the School for their responses to my
requests for further information.
13. I have been provided with a substantial amount of information / data by the LA, and
the School. I have referred only to that which has a bearing on my determination.
14. There is no formal consultation required for a variation and so parents and others do
not have the opportunity to express their views. Clearly it is desirable that changes to
arrangements are made via the process of determination following consultation as the
consultation process allows those with an interest to express their views. It also allows for
objections to the adjudicator. None of this is afforded by the variation process.
15. I note here that the arrangements for 2027/28 have been determined. This means
that if I agree to the Admission Authority’s request to vary the arrangements for 2026/27 as
proposed, it will be for that year only and will not have a bearing on subsequent years.
Consideration of proposed variations
16. Paragraph 3.6 of the Code (as above) requires that admission arrangements, once
determined, may only be revised, that is changed or varied, if there is a major change of
circumstance or certain other limited and specified circumstances. I will consider below
whether the proposed variations are justified by the change in circumstances.
17. For both 2025/26 and 2026/27, the PAN in the determined arrangements is 60
children. The Admission Authority has proposed that the PAN for children currently in
Reception Classes, admitted in 2025/26, be reduced to 40. There are currently 36 children
in that cohort. For clarity, the PAN applies to the maximum number of children the School
can be required to admit in the September of the admission year, and in-year while the
children are in the year of admission. The Admission Authority has further proposed that the
PAN for children about to be admitted to Reception Classes in 2026/27 be reduced to 20.
This reflects a low number of places allocated for September, 17 children.
18. The maximum number of places which could be admitted to Reception by the School
in 2025/26 was set by the PAN of 60. However, the effect of the PAN expires at the end of
that academic year. From that point onwards, the capacity of classes in the cohort in Year
3

1, is set by the class organisation of the School. The major factors on that assignment are
the class size limit of thirty children, due to infant class sizes legislation (as set out in The
School Admissions (Infant Class Sizes) (England) Regulations 2012 and in paragraph 2.16
of the Code), and the willingness of the School to create viable mixed aged classes. The
School has already created mixed aged classes for children in Years 1 and 2, which gives it
considerable flexibility.
19. Regarding the requested variation of the PAN for 2025/26 to 40 places, in my
judgement it is hard to find this to be necessary nor significant. The determinant of
availability of places in that cohort, which will be Year 1 in 2026/27, is not its PAN on
admission, but the number of classes and the number of children in those classes. The
School could not legitimately deny places into Year 1 next academic year on the basis of
the PAN used for that cohort of students when admitted in 2025/26. However, there is no
reason not to agree this variation at this stage in the school year and I agree that the PAN
for 2025/26 can be 40.
20. I will now consider the variation for 2026/27. The School is one of four schools
admitting children to Reception in Romsey, which is a sub-area of the admissions planning
area. The other schools are Cupernham Infants School, Halterworth Primary School and
Romsey Abbey Church of England Primary School. These schools are less than one mile in
distance from the School, which is situated in the centre of the triangle which they form. A
further school, North Baddesley Infant School, is too far distant from the School to be
relevant to this adjudication.
21. Of the four schools in consideration, only Romsey Abbey is generally oversubscribed
and admits up to its PAN of 30. For the other schools for admission in 2026/27, the places
allocated are the School (17 places offered, PAN of 60), Cupernham (66 offers for a PAN of
90), and Halterworth (56 offers for a PAN of 60). For transparency North Baddesley is also
under-subscribed for September 2026 entry to Reception.
22. The LA has a duty to ensure that there are sufficient places for the children in its
area. To fulfil this duty the LA assesses the likely future number of places to be needed and
plans to meet that need. The LA uses planning areas, which are geographical areas and
the schools within those areas, for this purpose. In the planning area for the School there
are 330 places available on determined arrangements for September 2026, but only 250
offers have been made. The LA has stated, “Offers for this school are currently low, and
overall demand within the school place planning area remains below capacity. It is therefore
not expected that any applications will be frustrated. In the unlikely event that this does
occur, there is adequate capacity elsewhere within the local planning area. The Local
Authority would not support this application if this were not the case.”
23. The effect of granting the variation for 2026/27 would be to reduce the number of
places available in the admissions planning area in September 2026 to 290. No child would
lose their allocated place at the School. Three other schools in Romsey would still be able
to admit additional children to Reception in-year in 2026/27. The location of the School is
such that no significant additional journey would be likely to be necessary.
4

24. The LA has stated that its reason for seeking the variation is that the School is
operating well below capacity which is creating significant operational and financial
pressure. Aligning the PAN more closely with the school’s realistic intake is therefore
necessary to ensure efficient class organisation and to avoid the financial pressures
associated with maintaining capacity significantly above expected numbers.
The LA has provided the following projected School organisation for September

25. At first review, these figures look plausible for 2026/27. They could be achieved by a
PAN variation to 20. However, that variation would bind the School to offer up to 20
Reception places either for September or for in-year entry in 2026/27 although the
Admission Authority can admit over PAN as provided in paragraph 1.4 of the Code.
26. That would then have consequences for the age profile of the two mixed aged KS1
classes in 2027/28. If 20 Reception aged children progress into Year 1, this limits the
school’s ability to recruit Year 2 aged children into those mixed aged classes – and this age
group is where the local need may be.
27. I note the LA assumes two classes of 30 at the School in Reception in 2027/28. This
is not a plausible assumption. It is challenging to see why the LA would make this
assumption given historic and projection data. The School has not exceeded an intake of
37 in terms of children admitted to Reception in the last three years. The LA projection for
2026 Reception need at the School was 33 places, but only 17 places have been allocated.
The LA projection for need for 2027 Reception entry is only 36 places, with a determined
PAN is 60.
28. The implication is that I cannot judge the savings suggested for 2027/28 as well-
founded. What appears to be a valuable saving of £250,000 may not be plausible, and in
any event, still leaves the School with a large budget deficit.
7

29. I offered the LA the chance to provide alternative figures for the future using a more
plausible and lower PAN in 2027/28. Such a PAN would only operate if the authority chose
to submit a further request for revision for the 2027/28 arrangements. The LA has not done
so. As adjudicator I therefore have uncompelling information of the likely real-world financial
outcome of the variation requested for 2026/27.
30. This creates an unusual decision problem for the adjudication. On one hand I need
to judge the adverse effect of the change requested compared to benefits of agreements.
31. I have considered the impact of decreasing admission numbers on school finances
balanced against the impact reducing the School’s PAN will have on meeting parental
preference. Parents have a right to express a preference as to where their children go to
school. However, admission authorities cannot give any guarantee that preferences will be
met. Additionally, infant class sizes are limited to 30 (as set out in The School Admissions
(Infant Class Sizes) (England) Regulations 2012 and in paragraph 2.16 of the Code). The
cost of a teacher and the resources necessary for an infant class, when compared to, say, a
junior or secondary school teacher / class (where numbers are not limited), has to be borne
by proportionately smaller income from the children admitted to infant classes.
32. I have tried to ensure that I have considered the competing needs of providing the
school places that parents want for their children and the financial viability of the School.
33. In this request I can see no adverse effects from the changes requested.
34. The LA is satisfied that it will have adequate capacity for Reception entry in the rest
of the decade, even using figures for the need for places which are unrealistically high for
2026/27.
35. No first preference applicants for the School will lose allocated places if the variation
for 2026/27 is agreed. Alternative schools admitting to Reception are in any event nearby.
36. The School already has expertise in running a mixed-age curriculum. In some cases,
allowing the variation for 2026/27 will allow some use of single age classes, an equally
successful form.
37. In contrast there will be a limited financial benefit to the LA and the School. Money
will be saved, albeit to a limited and in some ways inadequately identified degree. Granting
the variation for 2026/27 would however eliminate a long-standing mismatch between
places available in Reception in the admissions planning area and the need for those
places, which I believe to aid future planning. The LA specified this as an objective.
38. On balance I therefore agree to the requested variations for both 2025 and 2026.
39. It will be for the LA and School to work together to determine future arrangements in
the way expected by the Code. The LA advised the School to agree to go to consultation on
its arrangements in both 2024 and 2025, and the School declined. In the short run the LA
may seek a further request for variation of PAN for 2027/28. I cannot pre-judge how the
OSA would determine such a request.
8

Determination
In accordance with section 88E of the School Standards and Framework Act 1998, I
approve the proposed variation to the admission arrangements determined by
Hampshire County Council for Romsey Primary School and Nursery, for 2025/26 and
for 2026/27.
I determine that for admission in 2025 the published admission number shall be 40.
I determine that for admission in 2026 the published admission number shall be 20.
Dated: 10 July 2026
Signed:
Schools Adjudicator: Patrick Storrie
